metadata.project: Chicago Taxi Shift Research — evidence base for shift_summary.sqlx business rule
metadata.method: Two independent web-research lanes (official/regulatory + industry/academic/historical), cross-checked and deduplicated. Raw re-crawl possible via chicago_taxi_shift_research.py.
negative_findings: No definition of 'shift' in MCC 9-112-010; 'shift' appears in code only as '12 hour shift' / '24 hour shift' lease units.
No Chicago source (law, BACP rules, news, academic) documents a specific day/night changeover clock time for Chicago. NYC 4-5pm/5am windows are comparative only.
Dataset has no driver identifier; taxi_id is a medallion-level vehicle identifier (Data Portal metadata).
No Illinois state statute sets Chicago taxi shift hours (home-rule city; BACP/MCC Title 9 governs).

sources.title: Municipal Code of Chicago 9-112-230 — Tiered lease rate structure
passages: "$74 per 12 hour shift" ... "$518 total for seven consecutive 12 hour shifts" ... "$101 per 24 hour shift" ... "$707 total for seven consecutive 24 hour shifts" (Tier 1)
"(d) No person shall charge more than the 24-hour lease rate by entering into two consecutive 12-hour daily leases with the same driver."
sources.proves: City economic regulation uses the 12-hour shift / 24-hour shift as the lease unit (B/C/E).
sources.does_not_prove: Any fixed clock-time start/end for shifts.

sources.title: Municipal Code of Chicago 9-112-250 — Restriction on consecutive hours of operation
sources.date: added Coun. J. 1-18-12; amended 6-6-12; in force ~Jul 2012
passages: "no chauffeur operates a taxicab for more than 12 consecutive hours within a 24 hour period"
"chauffeurs rest or refrain from operating a taxicab for a period of 8 consecutive hours prior to the start of a 12 hour lease"
"If a licensee enters into a 24 hour lease ... that chauffeur is resting or refraining from operating a taxicab after a 12 hour consecutive shift for a minimum of 8 consecutive hours"
sources.proves: Statutory 12h max continuous operation + 8h rest, effective before dataset start (covers 2013-2023). A '24-hour lease' is NOT 24h of driving.
sources.does_not_prove: Any schedule of shift start times.

sources.title: Municipal Code of Chicago 9-112-010 — Definitions
passages: Defines Chauffeur, Licensee, Taxicab, Owner-Operator etc.; no definition of 'shift' appears.
sources.proves: Negative finding: 'shift' is not a defined legal term in the taxi chapter.

sources.title: BACP Rules and Regulations for Taxicab Medallion License Holders
passages: "'12-hour lease' means a taxicab lease for a duration of 12 hours. '24-hour lease' means a taxicab lease for a duration of 24 hours. Two consecutive 12-hour leases shall be considered a 24-hour lease..."
Rule 8.06 Maximum rates: 12-Hour Lease $57.00; 24-Hour Lease $78.50
sources.proves: 12h/24h lease-shift structure predates the 2012 reform — continuity into the 2013 dataset start.

sources.title: BACP Taxicab Medallion License Holder Rules (2015)
passages: "servicing passengers using wheelchairs at least two times for every twelve hour shift worked"
sources.proves: BACP rule language continues to use 'twelve hour shift' as the standard work unit (B/E), mid-window.

sources.title: BACP Taxi Industry Notice 12-004 — New Taxicab and Public Vehicle Ordinances
passages: "A limitation to no more than 12 consecutive hours of driving each day for drivers, in line with federal motor vehicle safety laws and industry standards (a twenty-four hour lease option still exists)."
"'Weekly Lease' is the corresponding 12-hour or 24-hour shift rate multiplied by 7 days."
sources.proves: City frames the 12h cap as a driver-hours safety limit aligned with federal hours-of-service concepts (B).
sources.does_not_prove: A fixed schedule. (HTTP 403 on direct fetch; text captured via search index of the PDF.)

sources.title: Chicago Data Portal — Taxi Trips (2013-2023) dataset metadata
passages: "Taxi trips from 2013 to 2023 reported to the City of Chicago in its role as a regulatory agency. To protect privacy but allow for aggregate analyses, the Taxi ID is consistent for any given taxi medallion number but does not show the number..."
"times are rounded to the nearest 15 minutes"
Column taxi_id: "A unique identifier for the taxi." (~9,806 distinct taxi_ids, ~211.6M rows)
sources.proves: taxi_id is a medallion/vehicle identifier (C), NOT a driver; timestamps are 15-min rounded.

sources.title: City of Chicago Uniform Taxicab Lease Agreement (eff. 2020-01-01) + BACP Rule TX9.02
passages: Lease types: "12 Hour Daily Lease / 24 Hour Daily Lease / 12 Hour Weekly Lease / 24 Hour Weekly Lease"
"Daily Shift: ______ Start Time (HH:MM) ... End Time (HH:MM)" (blank field on the official form)
"RULE TX9.02 - 12 hour weekly leases must be for the identical shift time for all 7 consecutive days."
sources.proves: Shift start/end clock times are contractually negotiated per lease; the City mandates duration and consistency, not a citywide schedule. Strongest evidence that no mandated changeover time exists.
sources.does_not_prove: What times operators actually choose (not centrally documented).

sources.title: BACP Public Chauffeur Rules (2016 and 2025 editions)
passages: Chauffeur licensing/training requirements; no hours-of-service or shift-schedule rule appears.
sources.proves: Negative finding: chauffeur licensing rules contain no shift mandate; driver hours governed only by MCC 9-112-250.

sources.title: Illinois Commerce Commission jurisdiction — negative finding
passages: ICC regulates livery/limousine for-hire carriers under the Illinois Vehicle Code, not Chicago taxicabs (home-rule city; taxi authority delegated to Chicago BACP).
sources.proves: No state-level shift rule exists for Chicago taxis; municipal code is the governing authority.

sources.title: Frechette, Lizzeri & Salz — Frictions in a Competitive, Regulated Market: Evidence From Taxis (AER 2019)
passages: "most day shifts start around 5AM and most night shifts around 5PM"
"most day shifts ending at 4PM"
"the shift changes occur from 5AM to 7AM and 3PM to 5PM"
sources.proves: NYC benchmark: 5AM/5PM lease boundaries with measured 4-5pm and 5-7am transition periods (B/C/E).

sources.title: Farber — Why You Can't Find a Taxi in the Rain (QJE 2015 / NBER w20604)
passages: "a driver leases a cab for a fixed period, usually a 12-hour shift"
"Daily leases typically run for twelve hours, with two such shifts per day. The 'day shift' runs from very early morning to mid- to late afternoon..."
"shifts that start between 4AM and 9:59AM as day shifts (44.5 percent)... between 2PM and 7:59PM as night shifts (42.4 percent)"
sources.proves: 12h two-shift structure plus a defensible empirical day/night start-hour segmentation for trip data (E).

sources.title: Schmidt — Valuing Flexibility: A Model of Discretionary Rest Breaks (JMP)
passages: "rent for either the day shift (5 AM to 5 PM) or the night shift (5 PM to 5 AM)"
"almost all rental agreements between taxi fleets and drivers start or end at 5 AM or 5 PM"
sources.proves: The single most explicit 05:00-17:00 / 17:00-05:00 statement found — NYC only.

sources.title: Buchholz, Shum & Xu — Rethinking Reference Dependence (taxi labor supply)
passages: "day-shift drivers are required to return cars to bases... by 4-5pm for the evening shift, and night-shift drivers are required to return the car by 4-5am"
sources.proves: NYC measured handoff windows 4-5pm / 4-5am (C).

sources.title: NYT — Where Do All the Cabs Go in the Late Afternoon?
passages: "From 4 to 5 p.m., the traditional hour for cabs to change shifts, the number of active taxicabs on the streets falls by nearly 20 percent"
"Many taxicabs are used by two drivers a day, each working a 12-hour shift... owners schedule the shift change in the middle of the afternoon, so each shift gets a rush hour."
sources.proves: Documented 'witching hour' phenomenon and the rationale for mid-afternoon changeover (B/C).

sources.title: Bruno, Schneidman & Hewitt — Driven Into Poverty: Chicago taxicab industry study (UIC Labor Education Program)
passages: "The average shift is more than 13 hours. Chicago taxicab drivers as a group averaged 13.05 hours per shift"
"74.54 percent working 12 hours or more per shift"
"Taxicab drivers work 25 shifts per month"
sources.proves: Chicago driver shift durations cluster at/above 12h, consistent with the 12h lease economy (B). Pre-dataset era (2008 survey) but structurally continuous.

sources.title: NelsonNygaard for City of Chicago — Taxi Fare Rate Study (announcement)
passages: "eight months of trip-by-trip records for more than 10.6 million taxi trips conducted from January 1, 2013 thru August 31, 2013 provided by 3,900 taxis"
"'Extended-time drivers,' the 40 percent of drivers who work 11 or more hours a day, earn $12.50 an hour"
"20 percent... 'part-time drivers' that work 7 hours or less per day"
sources.proves: City-commissioned study on 2013 Chicago trip data confirms large 11+h driver cohorts inside the project window (B/E).

sources.title: CBS Chicago — Some Chicago Cabbies On Strike As New Rules Take Effect
passages: "new regulations also restrict cabbies to working no more than 12 hours a day, excluding breaks"
"most drivers need to work 8 hours a day, just to break even"
sources.proves: Contemporaneous confirmation the 12h cap took effect 2012 (A/B). '8 hours' is break-even economics, NOT a shift structure.

sources.title: Chicago Tribune (mirror) — 2 Cab Companies to Boost Drivers' Leases
passages: "cabdrivers rent taxicabs from the companies for 12-hour, 24-hour or weekly periods, paying a set fee."
"A driver of a Yellow cab who rents a cab from the company during the day will see his rate go to $63.59"
sources.proves: 12h/24h lease structure and day/night rate differentiation existed in Chicago by 1990 (B/C).

sources.title: Checker Taxi Co. v. National Production Workers Union (N.D. Ill. 1986)
passages: "Leases are given on a day, night or twenty-four hour basis"
sources.proves: Chicago day/night/24h lease triad predates Uber by decades (B/C).

sources.title: Luedke — Driving Lives: An Ethnography of Chicago Taxi Drivers
passages: "claiming the cab for a certain amount of time (12 hours, 24 hours, a week)"
"seven-days-a-week, twelve-hours-a-day labor"
sources.proves: Qualitative Chicago confirmation of the 12h lease as the dominant work unit (B).

sources.title: Schaller Consulting — Higher Pay, Safer Cabbies
passages: "returning to a central garage to pick up and drop off the vehicle at the start and end of each 12-hour shift"
sources.proves: Industry-standard 12h garage-shift lease model (B/C), NYC.

sources.title: MDPI ISPRS IJGI — Spatiotemporal Analysis of Taxi-Driver Shifts Using Big Trace Data (Wuhan)
passages: "The occurrence time of taxi-driver shifts in Wuhan mainly has two high peak periods: 1:00 a.m. to 4:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m."
sources.proves: Data-driven shift-change detection from trip/trace data is established methodology; changeover peaks cluster in early morning + late afternoon (E).

sources.title: J. Computer Applications (Fuzhou) — Time-space distribution identification of taxi shift
passages: "the identified taxi shift time is mainly from 4:00 to 6:00 in the morning and from 16:00 to 18:00 in the evening"
sources.proves: Corroborates ~4-6am / ~16-18pm changeover clustering via independent method (E).

sources.title: Camerer, Babcock, Loewenstein & Thaler — Labor Supply of New York City Cabdrivers (QJE 1997)
passages: "they rent these cabs for twelve-hour shifts to drivers who... typically paid $76 for a day shift and $86 for a night shift"
sources.proves: Foundational 12h + day/night rate differential documentation (B), NYC.

sources.title: City of Chicago — New Laws That Will Provide Financial Relief to the Taxicab Industry
passages: "An independent taxicab may be leased to a City of Chicago licensed taxicab driver..."
sources.proves: Post-Uber regulatory easing context (C); no shift-structure change.

sources.title: WBEZ — Study: Chicago cabbies earn average of $12/hour
passages: "full-time drivers who hustle 51 hours each week net an average $111 per day"
"Extended-time drivers who work 75 hours each week netted $120 a day"
sources.proves: Secondary coverage of the 2014 city study; long weekly hours imply 10-12h+ days (B).

sources.title: AutoMarketplace — The Real Economics of an NYC Taxi Medallion
passages: "why he and his father abandoned traditional day-night shift splits due to lost trips during driver handoffs"
sources.proves: Supplementary only: some operators abandoned two-shift splits in the late TNC era — caveat for late-window (2019-2023) rows.
